tools.name: list_websites
tools.description: List all websites in the authenticated workspace, newest first.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List the pages registered under a website. Each row's `id` is the pathId/targetPathId every other tool takes: pass it to run_scan to audit that page instead of the domain root, or to track_keyword/set_keyword_target_page to say which page a keyword should rank for.

tools.name: add_pages
tools.description: Register pages on a verified website so they can be scanned and targeted by keywords. Takes paths or absolute URLs on the website's own host — the site's sitemap is the usual source. Partial by design: `added` holds the registered pages (use their `id` as pathId/targetPathId), `skipped` says why eac

tools.name: list_scans
tools.description: List scans for a website, newest first.

tools.name: get_scan
tools.description: Fetch a single scan by id. Defaults to the summary view: scores, per-category pass/warn/fail counts, the ranked top issues and — when the page has a keyword mapped to it — how it scored against that keyword. Enough to decide what to fix. Pass view="checks" for every individual check, or view="full"

tools.name: run_scan
tools.description: Start a new scan for a website. An unverified website can scan its domain root (homepage) only; registered pages need domain verification. Returns immediately with a pending scan; poll get_scan or call wait_for_scan for the report.

tools.name: wait_for_scan
tools.description: Wait (up to ~45s) for a scan to finish, then return it in the same views as get_scan (summary by default). If it is still running when the wait elapses, returns the current pending state — call again to keep waiting. A scan of a slow page can take a couple of these.

tools.name: list_keywords
tools.description: List the keywords tracked for a website, with search volume, difficulty, CPC and Search Console metrics where known. tools.name: track_keyword
tools.description: Track a keyword for a website. Metrics stay empty until a research run prices it. Pass targetPathId to map it to a page — or targetRoot: true for the homepage, which has no page id of its own — and the next scan of that page grades it against this keyword. tools.name: untrack_keyword
tools.description: Stop tracking a keyword. Its metrics and page mapping are deleted with it. `keywordId` also takes an array to do several in one call; the other arguments then apply to every one of them.

tools.name: set_keyword_target_page
tools.description: Point a tracked keyword at the page it should rank for: a registered page by targetPathId, or the homepage with targetRoot: true (the root is always scannable, so it has no page id). tools.description: Backlink profile for a website: the latest snapshot (domain rank 0-1000, total backlinks, referring domains, broken backlinks, 0-100 spam score) plus up to two years of weekly history for trends. tools.description: Get a ready-to-use prompt describing what to fix in the code, built from a completed scan's report.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: add_pages, get_scan · Public sink: run_keyword_research · Destructive: run_scan, list_keywords, get_search_console_queries, track_keyword, run_keyword_research, get_usage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: add_pages, get_scan · Public sink: run_keyword_research · Destructive: run_scan, list_keywords, get_search_console_queries, track_keyword, run_keyword_research, get_usage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
